records.quote: Theorem 2.7. Let X, Y be two independent random variables having density functions fX, fY, cumulative distribution functions FX, FY, survival functions F̄X, F̄Y, respectively. Let T be a random variable with density function h and distribution function H. T is independent of X, Y. Then if 1. X ≥rh Y and either X or Y is IRHR then X^T ≥rh Y^T. 2. X ≤hr Y and either X or Y is DHR then X^T ≤hr Y^T.
records.family: General random variables under a common independent random shock (T-power transformation, X^T in the sense of Ebrahimi et al.)
records.compared: X^T vs Y^T under common shock T

hypotheses.text: (1) X ≥rh Y and either X or Y is IRHR
(2) X ≤hr Y and either X or Y is DHR

records.ambiguity: 'X^T' denotes the shock-transformed variable; superscript-T notation.

records.quote: Theorem 2.8. Let X and Y be two random variables. If X ≤hr Y and X or Y is DHR, then X ≤disp Y.

hypotheses.text: X ≤hr Y and X or Y is DHR

records.ambiguity: Background result attributed to Shaked et al.

records.quote: Theorem 2.9. Let X and Y be two random variables. If X ≤hr Y and X or Y is DHR, then X ≤LU Y.

hypotheses.text: X ≤hr Y and X or Y is DHR

conclusion.direction: X ≤_LU Y (less-uncertainty order, strengthening of Ebrahimi et al. Thm 2.3)

a_records.quote: Theorem 3.6. Let X1,...,Xn (Y1,...,Yn) be the set of continuous independent random variables having Xi ~ Gum(µi, σ) (Yi ~ Gum(µi*, σ)), i = 1, 2,..., n. Then, if (µ1,...,µn) ≻m (µ1*,...,µn*), we have 1. X1:n ≤disp Y1:n; 2. X1:n ≤LU Y1:n.

hypotheses.text: Xi ~ Gum(µi,σ), Yi ~ Gum(µi*,σ) independent; µ ≻m µ*

a_records.ambiguity: Two conclusions: dispersive order and less-uncertainty (LU) order, both via hr + DHR (Theorems 2.8, 2.9).

b_records.quote: Theorem 3.6. Let X1, ...., Xn (Y1, ...., Yn) be the set of continuous independent random variables having Xi ~ Gum(µi, σ) (Yi ~ Gum(µ*i, σ)), i = 1, 2, ...., n. Then, if (µ1, ···, µn) ≽m (µ*1, ···, µ*n), we have 1. X1:n ≤disp Y1:n; 2. X1:n ≤LU Y1:n.
b_records.ambiguity: Proof routes through X1:n ≤hr Y1:n and the DHR property via cited Theorems 2.8–2.9.

b_records.quote: Theorem 3.6. ... we have 1. X1:n ≤disp Y1:n; 2. X1:n ≤LU Y1:n.

conclusion.order: other: LU (less uncertainty order of Ebrahimi–Pellerey)
